name: Novacore Lumen Parka
description:
A mid-thigh insulated parka in a matte black technical shell, cut with clean utilitarian lines — no excess hardware, no decorative zips, just a storm placket, two hand pockets, and a single interior chest pocket. The insulation is a synthetic down-analogue rated to extreme cold. What makes the Novacore Lumen unusual is its integrated bioluminescent panel system: strips of engineered algae-film run along the shoulder seams and collar edge, producing a low, cool blue-white glow that the wearer can activate or suppress via a small pressure pad at the wrist.

Novacore markets this as a safety product — visibility in zero-light environments without requiring any power source beyond the algae's metabolic process. It reads differently depending on context. In the Shelf, the glow marks you as someone with money to spend on novelty. In Tier 3 and 4 spaces, it's a quiet flex — tech-adjacent but tasteful. Among the Spire crowd it's too understated to be interesting. The parka itself is genuinely excellent regardless of the glow feature.
functionality: Integrated bioluminescent shoulder and collar panels (algae-based, no battery required) — switchable via wrist pressure pad. Low-light visibility without powered illumination.
what_it_says: You have money for something interesting and you picked something that's still functional. You appreciate the intersection of biology and design.
worn_by: people who want subtle tech without looking like they're wearing a gadget
story_hooks: The algae panels in a batch of Novacore Lumens have begun glowing in a pattern that isn't random — the same sequence repeating across dozens of unconnected jackets, and no one at Novacore will explain why.
A character wearing the Lumen parka in a dark district finds that their glow is attracting something — not people — that seems drawn specifically to that frequency of bioluminescence.

Novacore's algae supplier has filed a complaint claiming the algae-film formulation was stolen from their proprietary strain — the legal battle threatens to pull every Lumen off the market and brick the panels in existing jackets remotely.
